description: Component: while release-v1.5-feature is loading, unavailable, or false, BillingConfiguration has no prepaid-alert card, spacer, heading, or changed surrounding order; when true, the card is between credit-expiration and external-credit settings.

Component: the card initializes credit currency from the client default, validates money and whole-percent inputs, disables client opt-in when no alert is enabled, and says the next check is the daily 09:00 UTC scan.

Action integration: read/update reject a disabled or unavailable feature flag, enforce their separate billing-settings permissions and tenant/client scope, and leave all policy columns unchanged on rejection.

DB-backed action integration: a valid partial upsert changes only the four prepaid-alert columns; invalid paired currency/amount, nonpositive amount, out-of-range percent, lowercase/non-ISO currency, and client opt-in without an alert are rejected without invoking broad null-delete behavior.
Migrated-DB integration: the new settings checks accept each valid disabled/enabled combination and reject invalid ranges or unpaired credit fields using real inserts/updates.

Migrated-DB integration: alert/delivery composite tenant foreign keys and unique keys prevent cross-tenant references, duplicate dedupe keys, and duplicate per-alert channel/recipient deliveries; both tables are present in runtime and migration tenant metadata.

Migration integration: Citus distribution succeeds, required scan/claim indexes exist, defaults are inert, and down removes deliveries before alerts and then the four policy columns/checks without rewriting existing client data.
Unit: credit aggregation includes only non-expired rows in the configured currency, never converts or mixes currencies, and supports a consumed historical balance of zero.

DB-backed subscriber integration: no credit history produces no zero-balance alert; relevant history below threshold opens one; equality resolves it; repeated low scans deduplicate; recovery followed by another drop opens a new episode.
DB-backed subscriber integration: changing credit threshold or currency resolves the open alert with policy_changed and evaluates the replacement policy as a distinct episode.

Unit: bucket math uses minutes_used over total_minutes plus rolled_over_minutes, does not alert one unit below the exact boundary, alerts at equality, preserves observations above 100 percent, and skips non-positive capacity.

DB-backed subscriber integration: only current Bucket configurations owned through client_contracts -> contracts -> contract_lines are evaluated; unrelated clients, non-Bucket configurations, removed client_contract_lines relationships, and noncurrent periods are excluded.

DB-backed subscriber integration: repeated scans of one bucket_usage/configured-percent pair produce one alert, a new usage period is independently eligible, and a percentage change resolves/re-evaluates the old policy alert.

DB-backed concurrency integration: duplicate events and concurrent workers contending for one client create one logical alert and one delivery identity because the client lock and unique constraints converge.

DB-backed recipient integration: an active account manager gets a preference-aware high-priority internal delivery plus email when valid; an inactive, missing, or email-less manager is isolated and the email-less active manager still gets internal delivery.

DB-backed recipient integration: client delivery is absent by default, opt-in uses the canonical invoice-recipient precedence with recipientClientId, and an address shared with the manager yields one normalized email delivery retaining both roles.

DB-backed recipient integration: enabling client opt-in during an open alert adds only the missing client delivery; manager reassignment and recipient email changes do not resend any already-successful role delivery, but an unresolved role may be retried on a later scan.

Registry completeness: both email and internal subtypes exist for credit and bucket alerts, internal templates are warning/high by default, every billing-email locale is present, every msp/clients locale including xx/yy has settings copy, and links differ safely by recipient role.

Scheduling contract: CE registers only the prepaid-balance-alert-scan singleton at 0 9 * * * for each tenant, while EE skips that CE path and defines one 09:00 UTC global maintenance fanout schedule with overlap SKIP and the established catch-up window.

Jobs boundary contract: the prepaid scan handler rejects missing tenant context, publishes PREPAID_BALANCE_ALERT_SCAN_REQUESTED for a valid tenant, is registered in both the job registry and maintenance fanout, and has no server, PostHog, billing-orchestration, or notification imports.

DB-backed feature-flag guard: with release-v1.5-feature false, throwing, or unregistered, a scan against configured low credit and bucket data creates zero alerts, deliveries, internal notifications, and email-provider calls.

DB-backed lease integration: two drainers claim disjoint deliveries with SKIP LOCKED, stale processing leases are reclaimed, transient failures increment attempts, and the fifth failure becomes exhausted and remains auditable.

DB-backed delivery integration: internal notification insertion and sent status commit together and roll back together; a preference-disabled delivery is terminal skipped and replay cannot create another internal notification.

Delivery integration: email runs outside the database transaction, records sent after provider success, retains a retryable error after transient failure, and never exceeds the bounded retry policy; the acceptance-before-status crash window is documented as at-least-once rather than asserted exactly-once.

Observability integration: one tenant run with opened, deduplicated, resolved, skipped, retried, invalid-capacity, missing-history, and unroutable cases emits a complete summary and structured warnings containing identifiers but no raw email or template body.

Behavioral end-to-end: an authorized user saves both alert types and client opt-in from Billing > General, no immediate send occurs, the next enabled daily scan creates credit and bucket alerts, routes manager/client deliveries, and a second scan sends nothing again.

Tenant-isolation integration: a scan event for one tenant cannot read another tenant's settings, ledger rows, alert history, deliveries, users, or client recipients, and one client's query/delivery failure does not abort other configured clients.
